import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 2.45

by Yu. I. Merzlyakov

P. Hall conjectured that if the marginal subgroup of a word has finite index
$m$ in a group $G$, then the corresponding verbal subgroup is finite and its
order divides a power of $m$. The divisibility claim was refuted by
Yu. G. Kleiman; the finiteness claim remains open.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46),
Problem 2.45(b).
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.45»

/-- The verbal subgroup $vG$ is the subgroup generated by all values of the
word $v$ under assignments of its variables to $G$. -/
def verbalSubgroup {X G : Type*} [Group G] (v : FreeGroup X) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun f : X → G ↦ FreeGroup.lift f v)

/-- The marginal subgroup $v^*G$ consists of the elements $a$ such that replacing
any one argument $g_i$ of $v$ by $g_i a$ does not change the value of $v$, for
all assignments of the variables to $G$. -/
noncomputable def marginalSubgroup {X G : Type*} [Group G] (v : FreeGroup X) : Subgroup G := by
  letI := Classical.decEq X
  exact {
    carrier := {a | ∀ (f : X → G) (x : X),
      FreeGroup.lift (Function.update f x (f x * a)) v = FreeGroup.lift f v}
    one_mem' := by
      intro f x
      simp
    mul_mem' := by
      intro a b ha hb f x
      rw [show Function.update f x (f x * (a * b)) =
          Function.update (Function.update f x (f x * a)) x
            ((Function.update f x (f x * a)) x * b) by
        funext y
        by_cases h : y = x <;> simp [h, mul_assoc]]
      exact (hb (Function.update f x (f x * a)) x).trans (ha f x)
    inv_mem' := by
      intro a ha f x
      have h := ha (Function.update f x (f x * a⁻¹)) x
      simpa using h.symm }

/--
P. Hall's original conjecture asked whether, for every group $G$ and word $v$,
if the marginal subgroup $v^*G$ has finite index $m$ in $G$, then the verbal
subgroup $vG$ is finite and $|vG|$ divides $m^k$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
The answer is no: Kleiman gave examples for which the divisibility conclusion
fails.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.45».parts.b.variants.original : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (X G : Type) [Group G] (v : FreeGroup X) (m : ℕ),
      (marginalSubgroup (G := G) v).FiniteIndex →
      (marginalSubgroup (G := G) v).index = m →
      Finite (verbalSubgroup (G := G) v) ∧
        ∃ k : ℕ, Nat.card (verbalSubgroup (G := G) v) ∣ m ^ k := by
  sorry

/--
For every group $G$ and word $v$, if the marginal subgroup $v^*G$ has finite
index in $G$, must the verbal subgroup $vG$ be finite? This is the surviving
open half of P. Hall's conjecture.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.45».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (X G : Type) [Group G] (v : FreeGroup X),
      (marginalSubgroup (G := G) v).FiniteIndex →
      Finite (verbalSubgroup (G := G) v) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.45»
modeling_decisions: A word is represented by an element of `FreeGroup X`, and the theorem quantifies over variable types `X : Type` and groups `G : Type`. Every individual free-group word has finite support, so this captures words of arbitrary finite arity.
The verbal subgroup is the subgroup generated by all evaluations of the word under assignments `X → G`.

The marginal subgroup uses the standard right-insertion condition: an element `a` is marginal when replacing any assigned argument `g_i` by `g_i * a` leaves the word value unchanged for every assignment and variable. This condition is defined directly as a subgroup, with closure proved in the definition.

The numerical index `m` in the original conjecture is linked to `Subgroup.index` by equality, while `Subgroup.FiniteIndex` is separately required so that the infinite-index `Nat.card` convention cannot distort the hypothesis.
Finiteness of the verbal subgroup is stated explicitly as `Finite (verbalSubgroup ...)` before using `Nat.card` for its order.
The exponent in 'a power of m' is quantified as `k : ℕ`.

The original yes/no conjecture is recorded as `answer(False)` and tagged `research solved`, reflecting Kleiman's counterexamples; the surviving finiteness question uses `answer(sorry)` and is tagged `research open`.

  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ f : X → G, FreeGroup.lift f v = g}

/-- The marginal subgroup $v^*G$ associated to a word $v$. Its elements are those $a$ for which
inserting $a$ on either side of the value assigned to any one variable does not change the value

  letI := Classical.decEq X
  { carrier := {a | ∀ (f : X → G) (x : X),
      FreeGroup.lift (Function.update f x (a * f x)) v = FreeGroup.lift f v ∧
        FreeGroup.lift (Function.update f x (f x * a)) v = FreeGroup.lift f v}

      simp
    mul_mem' := by
      intro a b ha hb f x
      constructor

/-!
# Conjecture 2.45

by Yu. I. Merzlyakov

b) (P. Hall). Prove or refute the following conjecture: If the marginal subgroup $v^*G$ has
finite index $m$ in $G$, then the order of $vG$ is finite and divides a power of $m$.

*Editors' comment:* There are examples when $|vG|$ does not divide a power of $m$
(Yu. G. Kleiman, *Trans. Moscow Math. Soc.*, **1983**, no. 2, 63–110), but the question of
finiteness remains open.

Here $v = v(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is a word, i.e. an element of the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$.
For a group $G$, the *verbal subgroup* $vG$ is the subgroup generated by all values
$v(g_1, \dots, g_n)$ with $g_i \in G$, and the *marginal subgroup* $v^*G$ consists of all
$a \in G$ such that $v(g_1, \dots, g_i a, \dots, g_n) = v(g_1, \dots, g_n)$ for all
$g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ and all $i$. For the commutator word $v = [x_1, x_2]$ these are the
derived subgroup $G'$ and the centre $Z(G)$, and the finiteness question is Schur's theorem.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.45»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G] {ι : Type*}

/-- The verbal subgroup $vG$ of the group $G$ determined by the word $v \in F(\iota)$: the
subgroup generated by all values $v(g)$ of $v$ at tuples $g \colon \iota \to G$. -/
def verbalSubgroup (v : FreeGroup ι) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun g : ι → G => FreeGroup.lift g v)

/-- The marginal subgroup $v^*G$ of the group $G$ determined by the word $v \in F(\iota)$: the
set of all $a \in G$ such that replacing any single entry $g_i$ of a tuple $g \colon \iota \to G$
by $g_i a$ does not change the value of $v$, i.e.
$v(g_1, \dots, g_i a, \dots, g_n) = v(g_1, \dots, g_n)$ for all $g$ and all $i$. -/
def marginalSubgroup [DecidableEq ι] (v : FreeGroup ι) : Subgroup G where
  carrier := {a | ∀ (g : ι → G) (i : ι),
    FreeGroup.lift (Function.update g i (g i * a)) v = FreeGroup.lift g v}
  one_mem' := by simp
  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb g i := by
    have h := hb (Function.update g i (g i * a)) i
    simp only [Function.update_self, Function.update_idem] at h
    rw [← mul_assoc, h, ha]
  inv_mem' {a} ha g i := by
    have h := ha (Function.update g i (g i * a⁻¹)) i
    simpa only [Function.update_self, Function.update_idem, inv_mul_cancel_right,
      Function.update_eq_self] using h.symm

variable {G}

/-- The word $[x_1, x_2] = x_1 x_2 x_1^{-1} x_2^{-1}$ in the free group on two generators. -/
def commutatorWord : FreeGroup (Fin 2) := ⁅FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 2), FreeGroup.of 1⁆

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_one : verbalSubgroup G (1 : FreeGroup ι) = ⊥ := by
  simp [verbalSubgroup, Set.range_const]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem marginalSubgroup_one [DecidableEq ι] : marginalSubgroup G (1 : FreeGroup ι) = ⊤ := by
  ext a
  simp [marginalSubgroup]

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 2.45

by Yu. I. Merzlyakov

P. Hall conjectured that if the marginal subgroup $v^*G$ has finite index
$m$ in $G$, then the verbal subgroup $vG$ is finite and its order divides a
power of $m$. The divisibility claim was refuted by Yu. G. Kleiman, while the
finiteness question remains open.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.45»

/-- The verbal subgroup $vG$ is generated by all values of the group word $v$
in $G$. A word on variables indexed by `X` is represented as an element of the
free group on `X`. -/
def verbalSubgroup {X : Type*} (G : Type*) [Group G] (v : FreeGroup X) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun f : X → G ↦ FreeGroup.lift f v)

/-- The marginal subgroup $v^*G$ is generated by those $a \in G$ such that
replacing any input $g_x$ in any evaluation of $v$ by $g_xa$ does not change
the value of $v$. -/
noncomputable def marginalSubgroup {X : Type*} (G : Type*) [Group G]
    (v : FreeGroup X) : Subgroup G := by
  classical
  exact Subgroup.closure {a | ∀ (f : X → G) (x : X),
    FreeGroup.lift (Function.update f x (f x * a)) v = FreeGroup.lift f v}

/--
P. Hall's original conjecture asked whether, for every group $G$ and group
word $v$, if the marginal subgroup $v^*G$ has finite index $m$ in $G$, then
the verbal subgroup $vG$ is finite and $|vG|$ divides $m^k$ for some
$k \in \mathbb{N}$. The answer is no: Kleiman gave examples in which the
divisibility conclusion fails.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.45».parts.b.variants.original : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (X G : Type) [Group G] (v : FreeGroup X) (m : ℕ),
      (marginalSubgroup G v).FiniteIndex → (marginalSubgroup G v).index = m →
      Finite (verbalSubgroup G v) ∧
        ∃ k : ℕ, Nat.card (verbalSubgroup G v) ∣ m ^ k := by
  sorry

/--
For every group $G$ and every group word $v$, is the verbal subgroup $vG$
finite whenever the marginal subgroup $v^*G$ has finite index in $G$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.45».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (X G : Type) [Group G] (v : FreeGroup X),
      (marginalSubgroup G v).FiniteIndex → Finite (verbalSubgroup G v) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.45»
modeling_decisions: Represented a group word on variables indexed by X as an element of `FreeGroup X`, and evaluated it in G using `FreeGroup.lift`. Quantifying over arbitrary X is faithful because each free-group element involves only finitely many variables.
Defined the verbal subgroup as the subgroup closure of the range of all evaluations of the word.

Defined marginal elements by invariance of the word value after right-multiplying any one input by the element, and packaged the marginal subgroup as their subgroup closure. The marginal elements are mathematically known to form the standard marginal subgroup, so this closure has the intended value.

In the original variant, quantified over `m`, required both `FiniteIndex` and equality of `Subgroup.index` with `m`, explicitly required `Finite` for the verbal subgroup, and only then used `Nat.card` for its order.
Used `answer(False)` for Hall's refuted full conjecture and `answer(sorry)` for the surviving open finiteness question.
